methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $6M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Albacore is a seed-stage Ocean & Maritime company founded by John Huddleston and Dante Vaisbort that has raised $6.5M to date. The private comp universe for this sector remains sparse, with three identifiable private peers (Standard Subsea, Clippership, NetworkOcean) and no directly comparable public companies, limiting triangulation depth.

The valuation analysis relies on a stage-progression methodology, which is the applicable approach given data availability. Using total capital raised ($6.5M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage transitions yields an implied valuation of $16M. This reflects normalized expansion economics for the stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $14M to $19M, with a median point of $16M. The relatively narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodological anchor. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x multiplier for early-stage maritime/ocean ventures (which may face different capital efficiency curves than software or biotech), the quality of available private comps, and the absence of public benchmark data. Until additional financial performance metrics or later-round terms emerge, this range should be treated as preliminary and revisited with transaction or revenue data.
